short: Gustav Mahler, composer of symphonies and songs.
note: Gustav Mahler (1860–1911), Austrian composer and conductor whose works include large-scale symphonies and orchestral song cycles.

short: A British writer associated with supernatural fiction.
note: Oliver Onions (1873–1961), British novelist and writer of supernatural fiction. His collection Widdershins includes The Beckoning Fair One, about a writer and an uncanny presence.
Third from the end. Penultimate means second from last; ante- adds the sense of before.

short: A literary critic and co-founder of Partisan Review.
note: Philip Rahv, American literary critic and one of the founders and editors of Partisan Review, the influential literary and political magazine.

short: Possibly Rex Stout, the American mystery writer.
note: Possibly Rex Stout (1886–1975), the American mystery writer best known for books featuring detective Nero Wolfe and his assistant Archie Goodwin.
